title: CedarBank Private VPC discovery
next_steps: Send Private/VPC architecture diagram and required route table snippets
Schedule hands-on network runbook call with CedarBank infra (Priya + Daniel) next week
Provide cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private in us-east-1 vs eu-west-1
action_items: Alex Moreno - send architecture diagram and security docs - 2027-05-17
Priya Shah - schedule technical runbook session and bring sample terraform snippets - 2027-05-19
Marta Reyes - share current VPC peering and transit gateway config and approved IP ranges - 2027-05-18
summary: Initial discovery for CedarBank's Private/VPC deployment. Main focus: networking constraints (no public internet ingress for inference), cross-region replication, VPC peering vs PrivateLink/private endpoints, KMS/HSM for keys, SOC2 requirements, SSO/SAML, audit logs. SE clarified Redwood's Private offering (control plane split, data plane in customer VPC or appliances), discussed routing options (VPC peering, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink), NAT/egress, subnets, security groups, and required firewall rules. Agreed to a follow-up technical session to review terraform snippets and run a connectivity test plan.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for making the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this deal. quick intros?
[00:06] Marta Reyes: Hi, Marta here, Head of Cloud Infra at CedarBank. we're evaluating private deployments for regulatory reasons.
[00:12] Daniel Cho: Daniel, security architect. focused on key management and no public egress.
[00:16] Priya Patel: Priya, platform eng on infra that will run the inference workloads.
[00:20] Samir Iqbal: Samir, product, short on the business case side.
[00:23] Priya Shah: Priya Shah, SE at Redwood, I'll lead technical stuff.
[00:26] Tom Keegan: Tom from CSM, here to help with onboarding.
[00:30] Alex Moreno: Cool. high level: CedarBank wants to run Redwood Private in our VPC or on-prem? Marta?
[00:36] Marta Reyes: We prefer Private — must stay in our AWS account, no traffic crossing public internet. also need eu-west-1 region for some workloads and us-east-1 for others.
[00:46] Priya Shah: Got it. we support Private deployments where data plane lives in the customer's VPC and control plane in a customer-managed control plane or Redwood-managed depending on contract. for VPC patterns we typically do either VPC peering/transit gateway or AWS PrivateLink endpoints.
[00:58] Daniel Cho: We cannot accept peering that opens broad routing across our prod VPCs. transit gateway is possible but we need fine grained control. also, do you support interface endpoints or endpoint services?
[01:10] Priya Shah: We can expose a service as an AWS PrivateLink endpoint (interface endpoint) that you host in your VPC and connect from other VPCs in your org. alternatively, we can deploy the data plane entirely inside a dedicated VPC in your account and you control routing. both have tradeoffs.
[01:24] Marta Reyes: If we host it in our account, what network footprint do you need? subnets, ENIs, IP ranges?
[01:30] Priya Shah: Typical footprint: 3 private subnets across AZs for autoscaling inference pods, each needs outbound egress to Redwood control plane (can be via interface endpoints or NAT+proxy). we allocate elastic network interfaces for the service if using PrivateLink. IP consumption is modest — we recommend reserving a /24 per AZ as a conservative starting point.
[01:48] Daniel Cho: /24 per AZ is fine. about egress: we must avoid public internet routes, so control plane comms must go over PrivateLink or VPN. is the control plane able to live in their account?
[01:58] Priya Shah: There are two patterns: 1) split control plane — control plane in Redwood but connections from your VPC via PrivateLink and mTLS; 2) customer-managed control plane — fully in your account; typically larger enterprises pick the latter. for the split model, we can do mTLS with mutual certs and restrict endpoints.
[02:14] Samir Iqbal: What's the difference for latency/management between those?
[02:18] Priya Shah: Latency mostly affected by region placement and whether the data plane and control plane are in same region. The customer-managed control plane gives you full network locality and less cross-region hops. split control plane is easier to operate but requires secure connectivity.
[02:30] Marta Reyes: We also need KMS/HSM integration. can you use our CMKs?
[02:34] Priya Shah: Yes, customer-managed KMS keys supported. for HSM-backed keys, we have integrations with AWS CloudHSM and can support encrypting model artifacts and KV caches with your CMK. we'll need IAM roles that allow decrypt/encrypt for the Redwood runtime.
[02:48] Daniel Cho: Audit logs: we need access to all API calls and model usage logs, retention 7 years for some data. do you ship CloudTrail or do we consume logs in our account?
[02:58] Tom Keegan: We can deliver logs to your S3 or CloudWatch in your account via cross-account logging. Redwood also keeps audit logs for a configurable retention but for compliance you'll want the logs in your account.
[03:08] Marta Reyes: Good. about private endpoints — can you enumerate firewall ports? we are strict on allowed egress.
[03:14] Priya Shah: Sure, minimal set: outbound TLS (443) to control plane endpoints if using PrivateLink it's interface endpoints so it's within your network. For data plane peer to model store (S3) we use HTTPS to s3 endpoints; we support VPC endpoints for S3. Kubernetes control plane talk stays internal. TCP ranges for inter-node are ephemeral but we document port 10250/10255 for kubelet if needed, and our health checks use 8080/8443. We'll provide an exact runbook.
[03:38] Daniel Cho: Do you need NAT gateway or can you use VPC endpoints exclusively?
[03:42] Priya Shah: You can avoid NAT if you use interface endpoints for control plane, S3 gateway endpoints for artifacts, and PrivateLink for internal services. some customers still use NAT for OS updates and third-party package pulls; we recommend a dedicated egress VPC if you want to tightly control it.
[03:58] Marta Reyes: What about cross-region model replication? eu-west-1 to us-east-1. Any gotchas?
[04:03] Priya Shah: Model registry replication can be async. if you want low-latency inference, we recommend pinning model replicas in each region. replication needs S3 cross-region replication or we can replicate via our control plane transfer using encrypted transport; you'll need IAM permissions for cross-region S3 copy or inter-region VPC peering/transit.
[04:20] Samir Iqbal: For cost estimation, do you have guidance on Dedicated vs Private?
[04:24] Alex Moreno: Briefly: Dedicated is Redwood-managed reserved capacity (we host and operate GPUs for you) — lower ops overhead, fixed commit. Private is deployed in your account, more control, potentially higher infra ops cost. We'll send a side-by-side estimate.
[04:35] Daniel Cho: Another security point: SAML/SSO and RBAC for who can deploy models. we cannot have all engineers unrestricted.
[04:42] Priya Shah: We integrate with SAML/SSO identity providers and map groups to RBAC roles. When control plane is customer-managed, RBAC integrates directly with your IdP; with split control plane we do SCIM and SAML provisioning.
[04:54] Marta Reyes: About network isolation: we don't want inference traffic ever routing through our public load balancers. can the data plane sit in private subnets only?
[05:00] Priya Shah: Yes, data plane can be entirely private. for egress we can use VPC endpoints, and for ingress to your app we typically recommend internal NLB or ALB with private IPs. we also support direct peering to your app VPC via Transit Gateway or peering with route table restrictions.
[05:15] Daniel Cho: If we use Transit Gateway, do you attach on your side or we create attachments?
[05:20] Priya Shah: Typically customer creates the TGW attachments and shares the route table details; our deployment runbook includes Terraform modules you can apply. we prefer TGW for multi-VPC architectures.
[05:29] Marta Reyes: Do you have hardened AMIs or container images scanned for vulnerabilities?
[05:33] Priya Shah: Yes, runtime images are scanned, we publish SBOMs and CVE reports as part of enterprise package; we can push ECR images to your account if required.
[05:44] Samir Iqbal: Performance: what's latency like from app in us-east-1 to model in eu-west-1?
[05:49] Priya Shah: Cross-region adds typical network latency 70-120ms; we recommend region-local inference for user-facing low latency. for batch jobs cross-region is fine.
[05:58] Alex Moreno: Quick check — timeline? when do you need this in production?
[06:01] Marta Reyes: Regulatory compliance timeline is tight — aim for a pilot in Q3, production by Q4.
[06:07] Priya Shah: We'll propose a pilot plan: sandbox VPC deployment, run synthetic load, then compliance runbook.
[06:13] Daniel Cho: On encryption-in-transit, is mTLS supported end-to-end?
[06:17] Priya Shah: Yes, mTLS for service-to-service, and we support TLS 1.2+ with cipher suites aligned to your policy.
[06:23] Tom Keegan: Small note — we've also done SOC2+PCI customers with similar setups, happy to share references.
[06:29] Marta Reyes: Please share any runbooks that detail route table changes, security groups, and Terraform modules.
[06:35] Priya Shah: We'll share a repo with terraform modules and an architecture diagram.
[06:40] [transcript continues — technical deep dive Q&A with intermittent clarifications and slight transcription errors]
[07:00] Priya Shah: ...so, for PrivateLink endpoints you'll create an interface endpoint in each AZ and we will provide the service name to accept. that keeps traffic inside AWS backbone.
[07:12] Daniel Cho: Are endpoint DNS names resolvable to local IPs? we prefer split-horizon DNS.
[07:16] Priya Shah: Yes, interface endpoints resolve to ENIs in your subnets. we can also support private hosted zone entries if you need custom naming.
[07:26] Samir Iqbal: How do upgrades work for the runtime when it's in our VPC?
[07:30] Priya Shah: We provide rolling upgrades controlled by your schedulers; our operator runs reconcilers but we can schedule maintenance windows. you can pin versions too.
[07:40] Marta Reyes: Any firewall appliance requirements? we use perimeter NGFW that blocks unknown IPs.
[07:44] Priya Shah: As long as the NGFW allows the interface endpoint ENIs and the control plane IP ranges we provide, that's fine. we'll produce a minimal allowed list.
[07:55] Priya Patel: On IAM: will Redwood need cross-account roles?
[07:58] Priya Shah: Yes, usually one IAM role per region with limited permissions for S3 access and CloudWatch logs publishing; we provide least-privilege ARNs for you to approve.
[08:09] Daniel Cho: Does Redwood require any inbound public IPs for callbacks?
[08:12] Priya Shah: No, callbacks can be over PrivateLink or via your internal NLB. only tooling or external metrics export might need egress, which can be routed to your monitoring account.
[08:22] Alex Moreno: Let's call out metrics and observability — do you push metrics to our Prometheus or do you host them?
[08:27] Priya Shah: We can push metrics to your Prometheus remote write, or deliver metrics to CloudWatch. we support both.
[08:33] Marta Reyes: SLA concerns: if control plane is Redwood-managed, is there an SLA for control plane availability?
[08:38] Alex Moreno: Yes, enterprise contracts include SLA for control plane 99.9% and we have playbooks for failover. customer-managed control plane transfers SLA responsibility.
[08:48] [09:00] Daniel Cho: One more: do you support FIPS endpoints for crypto?
[09:04] Priya Shah: We can use FIPS-compliant KMS if required; some customers run in GovCloud with additional constraints — we can discuss separately.
[09:13] Marta Reyes: Ok, recap and next steps please.
[09:16] Alex Moreno: Recap: Redwood Private can run in our or your account, supports PrivateLink, Transit Gateway, VPC endpoints, customer KMS, audit logs to your account, SAML/SSO, and RBAC. action items: we'll send architecture diagram, terraform modules, SOC2/KMS docs. schedule tech runbook next week.
[09:35] Marta Reyes: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:37] Tom Keegan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[09:40] [call ends]

Notes about transcript: occasional speaker mislabels (Priya listed twice), some words transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "KMS" as "K M S" at times), natural speech, interruptions, and clarifications. Links shared: security whitepaper (https://redwood.example.com/security/whitepaper), private-vpc-runbook (https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/private-vpc), terraform-modules repo (https://git.redwood.example.com/infra/private-vpc-modules)
